free_tier.stated: VPS 1 at $7.10 per month: 15 GB SSD, 1 CPU, 1 GB RAM, 1 dedicated IP, Linux (AlmaLinux, CentOS, Debian, Ubuntu), billed per day, month or year, in the Netherlands, Slovakia or Serbia. The plan list is published at one price across the three locations, all described as Tier III data centres. The vendor's KVM page states 'Traffic for your VPS is unlimited. This means you can host services or applications that require a high bandwidth at no extra cost.' The price is recorded as $, not USD: the page declares 'priceCurrency': 'USD' in structured data whose low and high price (0.30 and 0.90, four offers) do not match this row, so the label is not established for it.

egress.terms: unlimited traffic in the vendor's words on the KVM page, with no allowance and no overage price stated; the tracker instead lists a 5,120 GB monthly figure
egress.free_allowance: unlimited, as stated on the vendor's KVM page

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
tooling: KVM with billing at bill.vps1.net; the site exposes a status page and an IP-pool page. No API was read.
chaining: Fifteen gigabytes of SSD, 1 GB of RAM and a claimed unlimited transfer for $7.10 across three central-European countries is a plausible always-on egress or relay point if the unlimited claim survives a test; the 15 GB disk is the wall that stops it being anything more.
limits_note: No monthly byte allowance is stated on either vendor page read; the KVM page states unlimited traffic outright. That conflicts with the tracker's 5,120 GB/month and 0.24 Gbps, and the conflict is left standing rather than averaged into a figure neither source gave. If the vendor's unlimited claim holds, the wall is the 15 GB disk and whatever port rate the plan actually has, which no vendor page read states.

evidence.proved: VPS 1 plan card, quoted cell by cell: '15 Gb SSD', '1 CPU', '1 Gb RAM', '1 dedicated IP', 'Linux operating systems', with the price block reading the dollar sign, '7.10', '/', 'mo'; the location selector offers the three options 'Netherlands', 'Slovakia', 'Serbia' and the page describes 'Tier III data centers in the Netherlands, Slovakia, and Serbia'
quoted: 'Traffic for your VPS is unlimited. This means you can host services or applications that require a high bandwidth at no extra cost.'

tracker row, cells in page order: '1 Intel Cores (shared)', '1,024 MB RAM', '15 GB SSD', '5,120 GB/month bandwidth', '0.24 Gbps port speed', 'IPv4', 'Netherlands', price '$7.10 / month'; repeated at the same price for Bratislava Slovakia and Belgrade Serbia

notes: The tracker's 5,120 GB/month and 0.24 Gbps appear on no vendor page read here, and the vendor's own statement is unlimited traffic, so the two are recorded side by side and the disagreement is the finding. The tracker also files this provider as 'vps1' while the domain is vps.one and the billing host is bill.vps1.net, which is why a name search on the dossier needs all three strings.
